messages.subject: Inlabru and segmentation fault
parts:
Dear all,

I want to change from INLA to inlabru but I face some difficulties:

a) the following code always yields: Segmentation fault and Error: C stack usage  21841048 is too close to the limit. What does this mean and how can I avoid it? 

data_early<-data.frame(y=temp_early$Rain_mean, long=temp_early$Longitude.cent, lat=temp_early$Latitude.cent, elev=temp_early$Elevation, months=temp_early$Month, years=temp_early$Year)

spde.nonstat<-inla.spde2.matern(mesh, B.tau=cbind(0, 0, 0, 1, values_on_mesh), 
                         B.kappa=cbind(0, 1, values_on_mesh, 0, 0),
                           theta.prior.mean=rep(0,4),#c(-4,0,4,0),
                          theta.prior.prec=rep(1,4))

lhood<-like(formula=y~., family="Gamma", control.family = list(link="log"),data=data_early )

formula4_mean<- ~ -1+Intercept(1)+lat+long+elev+field(cbind(long,lat), model=spde.nonstat, group=months, control.group = list(model="ar1"))

spde_fit<-bru(formula4_mean,lhood, options=list(               control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE,link=1),verbose=TRUE))

b) In case I want to do predictions of y at unobserved locations I should use the predict function right? But therefore I need the result spde_fit right?

and then it would be
predict( spde_fit, pred_data, formula4_mean, samples=100) ?

Very much looking forward to your answer.
All the best and thank you in advance,
Corinna

Dear Finn,

surprisingly it worked out with int.strategy="eb".

But now I still have problems with the predict function.
I want to predict the values Rain_mean at locations (dp$Longitude, dp$Latitude) with given covariates Longitude, Latitude and Elevation at these locations and AR(1) structure over month.

I tried the following: 

predict(spde_fit, cbind(dp$Longitude, dp$Latitude),formula= formula4_mean) #formula4_mean from above

and

predict(spde_fit, cbind(dp$Longitude, dp$Latitude),formula= ~-1+Intercept(1)+dp$Longitude.cent+dp$Latitude.cent+dp$Elevation+field(cbind(dp$Longitude, dp$Latitude), model=spde.nonstat, group=dp$Month, control.group=list(model="ar1")))

which does not work, but
predict(spde_fit, NULL) works. However, I need predictions at my predefined locations of dp.

Can you please help me with that.

Anyhow, thanks a lot.
Best,
Corinna

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Inlabru and segmentation fault
parts:
Please see the inlabru vignettes for proper component and formula
syntax, as it seems you're mixing different concepts; the component
definitions should use inputs that are defined in the data objects you
supply to like()/bru().
The prediction expression is a general R expression (after the "~").
It's just in some model definitions the predictor is implied to be the
plain sum of the component effects.

Since your model component definition used cbind(long, lat), you need
to supply long&lat and all other input variables in the prediction:

predict(spde_fit, data.frame(long=dp$Longitude, lat=dp$Latitude,
elev=..., months=...),formula= ~ Intercept+long+lat+elev+field)

Finn
